title: Password column cells display secrets in plaintext on screen
existing_state: Only the toolbar password box is masked (InitializePasswordMasking, Form1.cs:1599-1606 sets tsbPassword.TextBox.UseSystemPasswordChar). The grid's 'password' column — an explicitly recognized special column (Form1.cs:139) — renders values as plain text. Passwords are visible whenever the user types them (until the next environment load migrates them to Credential Manager per Form1.cs:2292-2303), and permanently visible when Credential Manager is unavailable or the CSV was just opened from disk. On a NOC workstation or during screen sharing, every per-host password in a loaded CSV is readable on screen.
recommendation: Mask the 'password' column display: in a CellFormatting handler on dgv_variables, replace non-empty values in the password column with bullet characters (display-only — underlying value untouched, so CSV save and execution are unaffected); let the editing control show the real value while a cell is in edit mode (the grid already commits on cell leave, Form1.cs:4310-4313). Optionally add a small eye-toggle in the column header context menu to reveal values deliberately. Keep the custom-paint path in mind: the grid uses CellPainting for checkboxes/headers (Form1.cs:4087-4205) but plain text cells render normally, so CellFormatting suffices.
user_benefit: Standard behavior for every credential-handling tool (mRemoteNG, SecureCRT, KeePass): secrets are not readable by shoulder-surfers or in screenshots/recordings of a multi-host run session.

evidence.note: Only the toolbar password textbox gets UseSystemPasswordChar — nothing masks the grid column
'password' is a first-class special column, so the app knows exactly which column to mask

mockup_idea: Before/after of the host grid with a 'password*' column: before shows 'Sup3rS3cret!' in each row; after shows '••••••••' with one row in edit mode showing the real value and a header context menu item 'Reveal passwords' visible.
